Manila Mayor Francisco "Isko Moreno" Domagoso and MMDA Chairman Atty. Romando Artes jointly inspect the mobile pumps stationed at the floodgate along Roxas Boulevard in Malate, Manila on Friday, September 26. 

Although Typhoon #OpongPH has yet to significantly impact the city, the pumps have been prepositioned to mitigate potential flooding. (Contributed photos)

Heavy Rainfall Warning No. 6 #NCR_PRSD
Weather System: Severe Tropical Storm OPONG
Issued at: 5:00 PM, 26 September 2025(Friday)

YELLOW WARNING LEVEL: Batangas and Quezon(Tayabas, Dolores, Sariaya, Candelaria, Tiaong, San Antonio, Lucena, Padre Burgos, Pagbilao, Unisan, Agdangan, Atimonan, Plaridel, Gumaca, Pitogo, Lopez, Calauag, Guinayangan, Macalelon, General Luna, Catanauan, Buenavista, San Narciso, San Francisco, Mulanay, San Andres, Tagkawayan).
ASSOCIATED HAZARD: Possible FLOODING in flood-prone areas.
Meanwhile, expect light to moderate with occasional heavy rains over Bulacan, Metro Manila, Rizal, Nueva Ecija, Tarlac, Pampanga, Zambales, Bataan and Quezon(General Nakar, Infanta, Burdeos, Jomalig, Panukulan, Patnanungan, Polillo, Alabat, Sampaloc, Mauban, Real, Lucban, Quezon, Perez) within the next 3 hours.
Light to moderate with occasional heavy rains affecting Cavite and Laguna(Alaminos, Bay, Cabuyao, Calauan, Calamba, Santa Rosa, Los Banos, Rizal, San Pablo, Binan, San Pedro, Victoria, Nagcarlan) which may persist within 3 hours and may affect nearby areas.

The public and the Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Offices concerned are advised to MONITOR the weather condition and watch for the next warning to be issued at 8:00 PM today.
For more information and queries, please call telephone numbers 8927-1335 and 8927-2877 or log on to https://t.co/59mTpZJq1n.
